increment_paragraph: **CALLBACK-CANDIDATE-LITERAL-PREMISE (2026-11-19).** User decision 2026-11-19 launches the follow-up OPENSSL-BIO-READER-INVOCATIONS recorded. Route G enforces a literal-argument premise (C04.5) at the calls of its declaration, but a callback candidate is a function designator whose actuals the invoker chooses, and the callback route classified it by its contract alone: a function-map candidate through callback_contracts::classify, a withheld one through candidate_composition, and a registration or constructed member registration by storing its contract. Gateway rule 57 is amended in place (C04.5 "At a callback candidate"): a candidate whose declaration carries a literal-argument premise, and every candidate under a poisoned premise set, has no contract in force wherever it is a candidate. The parser keeps the premise set route G read for the body; Parser::candidate_withdrawn classifies such a candidate Missing first in classified_in (before its contract, composition, hand-off or member paths), and Parser::candidate_contract stores no contract for it at a registration or a constructed member registration. The premise is never checked against an invocation's actuals. Route-only: no contract or lock changed. The card's fixture read every premise row Safe at base on all four paths (invocation, composition, registry, constructed member) and refuses each now, with premise-free twins still Safe; removing either registration guard alone makes its test read Safe again. Survey: seven shipped declarations could have been applied as candidates (flb_hash_table_add, cfl_kvlist_insert_bytes, cfl_array_append_bytes, fcntl, prctl, pthread_join, rd_kafka_topic_partition_destroy0); the OpenSSL readers and the rest were already effectful or uncontracted. Lean: new QCore.CallbackCandidatePremise, audited. Opt-in current over Fluent Bit 046accf6 (base main 062974679 vs tip 581e8f55a): 1098 Safe / 2 Pending / 3699 Unknown / 5 Unsafe in both, no row moved or changed content, bindings 113 all Pending, as predicted. Pinned routes were not runnable on the card's host (no build/cycle19): measure --declared deferred to the integrator.

ledger.title: A callback candidate's loop-owner, thread-synchronization or lifecycle obligation is not read at the invocation
ledger.text: Found by CALLBACK-CANDIDATE-LITERAL-PREMISE, pre-existing, out of its scope (literal-argument premises only). Route G refuses every call of a callee carrying a declared loop-owner (rule 10p), thread-synchronization or lifecycle obligation (rule 10q; LiteralPremises::loop_owner, thread_sync, lifecycle), but when the same function is a callback candidate the callback route classifies it by its contract, as it did a premise-carrying one before this card. Declarations carrying one: flb_start, flb_stop, flb_destroy (lifecycle); flb_input_collector_delete, flb_input_collector_pause, flb_input_collector_resume, flb_input_collector_running (loop owner); pthread_cond_destroy, pthread_cond_init, pthread_cond_signal, pthread_cond_timedwait, pthread_cond_wait, pthread_join (thread synchronization; pthread_join also carries a literal-argument premise and is withdrawn by this card). DISCHARGE: extend LiteralPremises::withdraws_candidate to the three obligation sets (Parser::candidate_withdrawn already reads it on every candidate path), with a fixture pair in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/callback_literal_premise.rs and the obligation in QCore.CallbackCandidatePremise's withdrawn. Size: small.

ledger.title: A constructor's registration of its callback parameter is not a store of the run's member closure
ledger.text: Found by CALLBACK-CANDIDATE-LITERAL-PREMISE, pre-existing, observed in a test harness only. qcore-audit's callback_member_fold::declared_stores turns a declared member registration into a parameter (CallbackClause::MemberRegistered) and a constructor's stated function default (MemberValue::Function) into stores of the run's member closure (rule 12n), but not a constructor's registration of its callback parameter into its result's member (resource_callback_member_registered(result, TAG.FIELD, cb), MemberValue::Callback). With the run's facts installed, an invocation of that member reads the run's closed set without the registered candidate. In the card's fixture (callback_literal_premise.rs's q_op_new / q_op_destroy, run facts built as declared_stores builds them) an effectful candidate registered through q_op_new read Safe (decide_run over an empty set invokes nothing), and refused without run facts, where rule 12o reads the constructor's registration (private log constructed-run-probe.log of the card). The one shipped instance, librdkafka's rd_kafka_op_new_cb, stores cb in its own body (rko->rko_op_cb = cb), which every measured Fluent Bit run reads, so the closure reaches its callers' actuals through that formal; a crate whose constructor body is outside the run would not. DISCHARGE: add a DeclaredStore for each MemberValue::Callback registration (the constructor, the callback's position) so the closure reads every call's actual there, with a fixture beside op_constructor_declarations.rs under run facts and Lean beside QCore.AppRkCallbacks; or show the closure already reaches it on the measured routes and record the boundary. Size: small.
